question: What is lenacapavir, and what did the US FDA approve it for in 2025?
text:
Lenacapavir is a long-acting antiretroviral drug. It targets the HIV-1 **capsid**, the protein shell that protects the virus’s genetic material, and disrupts several steps in the virus’s life cycle. ([accessdata.fda.gov](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2025/220020s000lbl.pdf?_sp=bb69ec9d-c2f6-4f5f-8707-dde8bb63783c&utm_source=openai))

On **June 18, 2025**, the U.S. FDA approved lenacapavir under the brand name **Yeztugo** for **pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP)** to reduce the risk of acquiring HIV-1 through sex. It’s approved for at-risk adults and adolescents who weigh at least **35 kg (77 lb)** and test negative for HIV-1 before starting. After the starting doses, it’s given by injection every six months. ([accessdata.fda.gov](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/220020Orig1s000Approv.pdf?utm_source=openai))

The 2025 approval was for **prevention**, not treatment. The FDA had already approved lenacapavir as **Sunlenca** in 2022, in combination with other antiretrovirals, to treat certain adults with multidrug-resistant HIV-1. ([accessdata.fda.gov](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/220018Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf?utm_source=openai))
